quest.title: An Introduction to Indoor Archaeology
quest.description: You have left the pit with the archaeological team. Now it is time to head over to the oasis Jebrael mentioned and get ready to camp there.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x40000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon never thought that there'd be such a place in the desert...

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: A gem on golden satin...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: It's quite safe around here, right? Ugh, I can finally relax.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Can Benben get wet? It shouldn't be a problem, right? Actually, let's just keep it away from water...

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: While Tirzad is resting, the rest set up a campsite.

talks.objective: Go high up to look for Jebrael

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It isn't anything important...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Whose gravestone is this?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Who knows. Maybe it belongs to a nameless researcher who once tried their luck like Tirzad, but didn't roll high like he did.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: King Deshret's secrets rarely reveal themselves to mortals.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Tirzad gave you the stone slate, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, how did you know?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Keep it safe.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is it important?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: You can't be unaware of its value, surely?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, its value to whom?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: ...To our employer, of course. After all, he is depending on it to write his paper.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Anyway, let's head back. We shouldn't keep Jeht and the others waiting for too long.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Jebrael, what do you think about these ruins?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: You should ask Tirzad. He's the professional here.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: ...I'm just a brute. All I know about King Deshret are old stories that no one wishes to hear.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #So, {NICKNAME}, I heard from Nachtigal that you beat up Stormterror and were made an Honorary Knight for that achievement?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Pardon me, but while you are quite skilled, are you really that powerful?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Of course! {NICKNAME}'s a hero in Mondstadt!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell them about your adventures in Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: That's amazing!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Well, books have been my only companions since I can remember, and I've never had the chance to travel far. Actually, this is my first time traveling so far from home...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Right, Tirzad's an Indoor... an Indoorsology researcher, eh? Wow, that sounds so lame.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Uh, I don't want to admit it, but my life has been bland if compared to all of yours.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Just like this desert. It's practically impossible for those who lack strength to find a single unoccupied oasis.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: If you're so unhappy, then why not do something else? How about being a traveling merchant like Nachtigal?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Or do something you're good at, like me and my father. That's not bad at all, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Haha, it's not that easy. I come from a family of academics, so I've been receiving training like this since I was a child.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Like how a farmer's son learns to farm, or a blacksmith's son learns to strike iron, while I'm not doing great and can't compare to the talented and established researchers of my family...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: But as things stand, I'm afraid I can't just do something else.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Uh, I guess I drank a little too much earlier. Why am I even telling you all of this? Well, just laugh if you want to.

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: I think you're being too stubborn. There's always a choice in life.

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: I mean, just look at Bonifaz and I. We weren't born as traveling merchants, and no one in our families has even been to Sumeru...

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: But we're still here with the northern wind at our backs. We don't regret our choice at all. Seeing the boundless world unfold before our eyes fills us with a sense of freedom.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Yeah, I, too, think that you're taking things a little too seriously, Tirzad.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Right, like the relative you mentioned earlier... Didn't she give up her family's rules, traditions, and everything else to live the life she wanted to?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Maybe she's somewhere in this very desert just like us, bathing under the milky white rays of moonlight and braving the dry night breeze while looking back at the great day she just had.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: *sigh* If only I had an iota of her courage...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I never knew making decisions would be this difficult because I've never given them any thought. I think I've lived the life I wanted for as long as I can remember.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's really...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Making choices is never easy.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Is that so?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Choosing one means giving up on the rest.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, is this like saying that there are ten tasty dishes in front of Paimon and that choosing one will make the other nine vanish? Oh no... If only there were ten Paimons to choose one each!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: It's like the branches on a tree. While they come from the same roots, their endless division makes it so that some may not touch each other for decades or even centuries.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Only when the entire tree withers and its trunk decays will those separated branches finally meet in the soil.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, why did you choose to leave the desert, father? You rarely mention your past, so I see all this very differently from Tirzad...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I don't have family traditions, and I don't even remember my mother's face. I only have you, and you only have me. There is no large tree and no branches that tie us together.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: You might have left the desert long ago, and this might be my first time seeing it for myself, but I have this feeling that we are like grains of sand here in the desert.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: No family, no objective... But what we are is pretty free. Haha!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jeht...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: The desert holds only the past. It has no future. If what lies beneath the sand and wind can be described as the truth, then I can only say that it perhaps isn't something that will bring joy to everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: I gave up the path of seclusion, not because it's a mistaken path, but because I found a better path. Jeht, I hope you'll be able to take that bright path.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I don't really understand you. If the path of sand isn't what you desire, then why accept Tirzad's commission? Don't tell me it's because you want to take a look at your past.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I think you just can't forget the desert and the hot winds that sweep it.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: The strange thing is that I have no memories of the desert, but coming here makes me feel like I've returned home all the same.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I love the sand, just like I love Paimon and Benben.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: This is a place with hope too. I'm sure of it. Isn't finding Benben proof of that?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hehe, it'll be a new day tomorrow. The ruins ahead are still waiting to be explored.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Keep your chin up, Tirzad! No matter what others say, I think you're a brave person. You've taken that first step and left the comforts of your home.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Now, just do as you've already done, and take the second step, then the third...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I'm sure you'll get to that place where no one has been, and find that... special research material of yours!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Huh... Even you can occasionally say some nice things, eh, Jeht?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Haha! I'm just speaking my mind. After all, I'm as free as the sand.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: But even the freest sand should rest at an oasis. It's getting late, so let's get some rest.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: I'll be on lookout tonight.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Heh! I'll sleep well with you on lookout, father.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You hear Jebrael softly and casually singing a peaceful tune as you fall asleep. Maybe it's an old local song.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
Tirzad
dialogues.text: *sigh* Camping out in the desert is terrible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, c'mon... Why are you being so negative again?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Well, the two of you are adventurers. Let's talk about you instead, Jeht. H—How can a young girl like you endure sleeping on the sand while dressed like that? I just can't figure it out for the life of me.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Tirzad, you're such a pampered guy. Tell me, will even a bean placed under ten mattresses disturb your sleep?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Of course not... Anyway, why would anyone sleep on ten mattresses?!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Haha! I don't know. Perhaps it might be a hobby of the wealthy, for all you know? But you should have expected that you'd have to camp outside. What else can we do, anyway? Go back the way we came?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Of course not! The material we gathered yesterday isn't enough to write anything good. Forget submitting it to the Akademiya, just reading it at the square would get me ridiculed.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Oh! Looks like you've still got some spirit, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: O—Of course! This huge ruin is right before me. It must be the Khemenu Temple! As a researcher, I must go in and have a look, right?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: And there is... is this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Benben?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Right, Benben... What a strange thing...

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep-beep!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Uh, I mean... Such an extraordinary thing might even be closely linked to King Deshret's civilization... If that's true, I can't turn a blind eye to it.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Going back the way we came would be worse than putting a bean beneath my mattress. You may as well have me sleep atop a hundred Benbens! I'd never sleep again!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...A hundred Benbens... Th—That really would hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Anyway, before I collect enough material for my paper... Ahem, I mean, until I figure everything out... I shall not leave.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I've paid all of you very well too, so... If we do encounter danger, I'm counting on you to earn that pay!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hey, come on, aren't we already companions on this journey? Of course we'll protect you in the face of danger — my father and I are professionals.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yeah! {NICKNAME} is amazing too! You have nothing to worry about!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Who knows what the future holds...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Better to be safe than sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Father?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: The merchants can rest in the oasis while we're away.

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: Gladly.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: We've discussed our contingency plans, but we must bury some of our supplies before we leave.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: In the worst-case scenario, the merchants may be forced to leave... This way, we'll still have some supplies to come back to even if that happens.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Is that really necessary?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Underestimate the sand and you'll pay with your life.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Since it's father, he definitely has his reasons. Well, it's always a good idea to prepare for every possibility.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You do as Jebrael says and carefully bury some supplies.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: This should do, right? Let's set out, then!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: S—Slow down... My hangover isn't...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Haha! Tirzad, you better hurry up, or someone else might publish a paper about this before you!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: ...Don't say things like that!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, you ready? Let's go too!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Huh? I thought it would be smooth sailing this time, but we still have to figure out a way to get the door open...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Isn't that good news? At least that means no one's ahead of me. Even if they may have chosen the same subject, I got here first!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: The Akademiya's researchers aren't alone in coveting King Deshret's relics.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: What do you mean coveting? I'm doing legitimate research, approved by the Akademiya! Don't you dare compare me to Treasure Hoarders!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's just find a way through the door.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Oh, {NICKNAME}, do you remember how Benben somehow made the stone slate light up?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's have a look at it. We might even discover a clue!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #Huh? What's Tirzad's stone slate doing with {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Well...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} here's an expert adventurer with much more experience in ruin mechanisms than Tirzad. Giving {M#him}{F#her} this important item will help us make the best use of it.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Ah! Yeah! That's it! That was my intention exactly!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Is that how it is? Fine, you do have a point.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #So, {NICKNAME}, have you figured anything out?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nothing so far...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Uh... Well, {NICKNAME} does know nothing about research.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: It's never too late to learn. You see, despite being well-read, I'm as clueless about this thing as you. I suppose I must continue improving myself.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: If I spend ten years working hard at the Akademiya...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Ten years of hard work won't do anything for a layman. Just forget it!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But you'll never know if you don't give it a try!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Wait, Benben's acting a little strange.

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep... Beep...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Maybe Benben can open the door?

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Bee-eep. Beep!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! It's actually opening up!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I didn't expect Benben to be able to do that...

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep— Beep!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hehe, I think Benben's saying that it's capable of more than that.

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon gets the feeling that Benben is much more useful than the stone slate... Or maybe we should ask this instead: Will this stone slate really be of any use?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Of course it will! It has to... I might lose my mind if it's of less use than Benben!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Be patient, it's too early to make any judgment yet.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Well, you're right, Jebrael! A shortsighted researcher is bound to amount to nothing! Patience is a virtue!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ugh... But neither Paimon nor {NICKNAME} are researchers...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well... That is true...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: That's enough. It doesn't matter who did it, all that matters is that the door opened, right?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Now that the door's open... You're eager to go inside, aren't you, Benben?

response.speaker: Benben
response.text: Beep! Bee-eep!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Alright! Tirzad Archaeological Team! Let's go!

response.speaker: Benben
response.text: Beep-beep!

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Let's advance with caution.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: #Oh, I know. We should be fine if we stay close to {NICKNAME}, right...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #C'mon, {NICKNAME}, let's get moving!

choices.text: I'm terrible at pursuing and waiting for things...

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Haha! But isn't life made up of exactly that?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, Benben's been milling around the door, but nothing's happening this time.

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep... Beep beep...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: It seemed to have been talking to the doors earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Stop that nonsense! Doors can't speak!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: But something like Benben shouldn't be able to speak either, right?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's true! Huh, guess Paimon's unknowingly accepted that Benben can speak as well... But can beeping really be considered speaking?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: As long as communication is achieved, it doesn't matter if the language used is something we're familiar with! For example, animals have their own languages, and the sand has its own language too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But if we don't understand it... Paimon's curious! Paimon really wants to know what Benben is saying...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Just ask Benben if you're curious! Benben, what were you talking to the door about?

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep... Beep-boop, beep, bee-eep! Beep beep... Beep!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Oh, I see.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Jeht, you understand it?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Haha! Of course not! It's just as I mentioned before, I can sense some of its emotions.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: But once you can understand Benben's emotions, trying to guess what Benben's saying isn't that difficult!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Well... To be honest, Paimon didn't sense or understand anything... {NICKNAME}, did you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Really?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hmm... Well, no one has been here in a very long time.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Oh, of course.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Someone has been here, but they weren't able to open this door.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, even Benben can't open it.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: The door is protecting something very important, and so much time has passed that it has almost forgotten how it used to open.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: People used to come here, long, long ago, and some would even pass this way many times a day.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: I mean, it's such a huge door after all. People used to walk here, huh? Hmm...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Oh, it must have been a mischievous cat that no one could catch, which is why so many people passed through here.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Huh? Wait a minute! Did the door tell Benben all of that?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Of course not. They're just guesses I made based on Benben's emotions.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: You... I—I almost believed you! If I had unknowingly included it in my paper, wouldn't everyone laugh at me once I publish it?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: H—How will you make it up to me when that happens?!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hahahaha! Tirzad, that would be your own mistake. As a researcher, you should be able to distinguish the authenticity of the materials you collect!

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Ugh!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (That was close! Paimon almost believed her too...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Thank goodness we don't have any papers to write.)

response.speaker: Benben
response.text: Beep?

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: We have a long journey ahead. Let's stop wasting time and get moving.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Right. This place is huge and filled with doors. If we do this in front of every door, who knows how long it'll take us to finish...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Wouldn't that be perfect? You aren't fond of camping outside, but this place has walls, a ceiling, and even the research materials you want!

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: King Deshret's civilization fell due to tyranny, and this place is probably his mausoleum. I'd rather spend two weeks in the desert than spend a single night here!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Uh, Tirzad, do you and King Deshret have...

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Jeht.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Oh, alright! Nachtigal and the others are still waiting for us at the oasis. Let's continue exploring!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, Paimon has no idea what Jeht's talking about...

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep... Bee-eep?

talks.objective: Explore the lower level of Khemenu Temple

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Ugh, I'm exhausted. Moreover, besides Benben, we haven't made any other discoveries, and that makes my exhaustion all the worse for it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? This place is huge, and we've seen so much on the way here! Paimon's sure there's a lot to write about, right? Even if Paimon doesn't really know much about these things...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Neither of you are a researcher, so of course you don't understand. What we've witnessed this whole time can only be considered as proof for existing research, except Benben...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: How should I explain this to a non-researcher...?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Let me put it like this: I want my paper to get approved by the Akademiya's review... It's like love!

choices.text: What does this have to do with love?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Let me explain!

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Ahem! A paper must stand out to pass the review. Just imagine that you're pursuing your ideal partner. If you're no different from the other candidates, then how will you capture their heart?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This analogy sounds like a real stretch, y'know...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: The way Tirzad thinks is really strange. In my opinion, a couple just has to consider each other suitable. There's no need to compete with others.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We're still talking about academic reviews, aren't we?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Ugh... I shouldn't have made that example. Just forget what I said!

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: I guess this is where our little chat ends. It'll be more efficient if we split up and look for clues.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: An archaeological expedition with no hope in sight. *sigh* Who cares about efficiency?

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: That stone slate has lit up once. We'll definitely find a way to make it light up completely. We just have to not give up.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: But how can you guarantee that? Wait, so you really do know something, don't you?

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: What I do know is that there may be hope if we continue forward, but we'll leave empty-handed if we turn back now.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Well... That is true.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Tirzad, stop worrying about this and that. An Indoorsology researcher like you has finally gotten the opportunity to enter some ruins, so just treat it as a chance to view some of your seniors' research subjects for yourself.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: #...You're right. I should be more professional. But even if we're going to split up, I want {NICKNAME} to stay close to me!

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: I'll have nothing to worry about with you around.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #Haha! There's no danger here! And while you might be a researcher, you're terrible at puzzles. You'll just be a burden to {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Exploring ruins has never been my forte! But if I'm given enough time... And pen and paper! Then such problems will be no problem at all!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Alright, alright. Anyway, just shout "help meeee!" if you're in danger or something...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: One of us will get there in time. Probably.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: What if none of you do?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: It's as impossible as breaking open ten bad eggs in a row for breakfast.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: I think you need some lessons in mathematics, Jeht... I can introduce a teacher to you once we return.

choices.text: I want to explore freely too, you know...

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Then we'll explore freely together!

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: The current situation is that I want to love it, but it seems to hold no interest toward me.

talks.objective: Return to the previous room and look for clues

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's strange! What's a ship doing in here?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Might it make sense because this is an "ocean of sand"?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Perhaps a river used to flow through here, but it dried up? Or perhaps... this boat was not made to be used by the living?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I'll have to head back and do some research on the geographical changes here to confirm my theory...

talks.objective: Try to unlock the rooms located deep within

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: *sigh* Benben seems to have a lot to share with doors. If only my father and I could do the same...

talks.objective: Try to unlock the rooms located deep within

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Have you found any clues? I haven't made any progress over here just yet.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Great! As expected of my assistant! No mechanism or puzzle shall ever be your match!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No need to exaggerate...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME} is impressive, but you should help out too, Tirzad!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, didn't you complain about being exhausted and not discovering anything so far? How are you this motivated now?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Ahem! It's because my researcher's intuition tells me that we're about to make a breakthrough!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Researcher's intuition?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is it like an adventurer's instinct?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Paimon gets it! That's the ability to predict that there will be an ambush at the corner or a trap behind a door, right?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #Then you'd better be careful, {NICKNAME}. Father, let's prepare for battle as well.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: What are all of you talking about? The researcher's intuition I mentioned is based on vast knowledge and careful observation. It's akin to a flash of genius!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: But what you've said does make sense. My consideration is lacking in that aspect. Well, if there's danger... I'll be counting on all of you to do the jobs I hired you for, then.

dialogues.speaker: Omid
dialogues.text: Phew, finally got the chance to put my feet up. I should really plan ahead for my next job now...

talks.objective: Enter the room located deep within

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: Let's take this opportunity to inspect our supplies... We've gotta use the Dusk Bird to send Bonifaz a letter and tell him we're safe now.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Is this... a mural?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Whoa! Haha! Bwahahahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Tirzad! Are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Me? Of course I am. I'm terrific! I've never felt better!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: #Since Paimon and {NICKNAME} aren't from around here, it's understandable that you don't recognize its worth.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: As for Jebrael and Jeht, uh... I guess it's a knowledge issue? No, it isn't something you should have knowledge about.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Paimon, let me test you for a moment. What can you discern from this mural?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, there are many people? And... and something like a sun and an eye...?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: *sigh* I guess Paimon has no talent for this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why did you even ask if you already knew that, huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: #And what about you, {NICKNAME}? What do you see in this mural?

choices.text: Hmm... It's a very symmetrical painting?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: It is symmetrical... But this isn't a matter of style alone. It symbolizes a solid structure, a rule by force.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: The sun and the eye symbolize King Deshret. Beneath him are the "seven pillars," so we call them, that hold up King Deshret's pyramid of authority.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: As for his subjects... They are insignificant. They dare not express any complaint. They are forced to submit.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: But even so, they couldn't escape destruction...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... Is that really the case?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Come now, how can I be wrong? The theme of this mural fully conforms to the depictions of King Deshret in everything I've ever read.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: A terrifying king who used absolute and supreme authority to keep all his subjects beneath him.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hmm... But this mural feels so peaceful to me. Everything feels so orderly, and everyone has their own place and duty. Isn't that good?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: What? What kind of crooked interpretation is that?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: ...Jeht, you can make up stories about Benben talking to doors, but deciphering murals and the history of King Deshret's civilization is my area of expertise.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: But...

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Now, I won't hear any buts. Everything I have said has been proven by prior research... and this mural will become part of Vahumana too.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Of course, I'll be the one to write it.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Jeht isn't entirely correct, but you... You know very little about the sand.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: #Ha! You've hardly said more than a few words all this time, yet you're standing up for your daughter now? I may not be a match for you in a battle of strength, but I have {NICKNAME} by my side!

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, you'll take my side, won't you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Uh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's not appropriate! We're all traveling together... No, we're all companions on this expedition. Even if our opinions differ, we shouldn't fight over it, right?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: What? Together? I started this expedition, and I paid for it. All of you are employed by me.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Moreover, I'm the only one with formal academic training. A layman has no right to speak on academic issues!

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: ...One who only draws from others can hardly call himself an independent researcher.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Oh? Then let's hear your "unique" insights.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: This destroyed kingdom was once strong and beautiful. It may be difficult to believe... that all of this was built in the desert.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: And you only see the obedience revealed on the surface, but fail to notice the direction of the people's hopes.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: It was their hope which tied the people of the sand to King Deshret. They thought this would help them overcome the calamity, but we know the outcome of that.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Heh, even delusions should have limits. Are you trying to overturn all prior research? I don't think there's sufficient evidence for any of this nonsense.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Well, what a coincidence. I, too, do not think that the opinion of a struggling researcher who came here out of desperation holds any weight.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Y—You...

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: I never knew you had such a sharp tongue...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Father...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Arguing won't change a thing.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly! Paimon can't figure out what you're arguing about, but if it's academic, there's always room for discussion, right? So, put your differences aside for now...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You can't convince each other anyway.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, so let's continue our investigation! Perhaps... Uh, perhaps we'll discover more clues, then we can see who is right and who is wrong, alright?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Ugh! This is infuriating! I shouldn't have discussed academics with a layman!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa! What's going on?!

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Whatever it is, it isn't my fault!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: This path looks like it leads upward.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: I don't see any traps.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon wonders where it leads... But staying here won't change anything either, so let's continue, shall we?

choices.text: Insignificant subjects and a great king.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Exactly! That's exactly what this mural symbolizes!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I wonder if a paper can be written from Benben and Jeht's interactions... But which field would it belong to?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: There still hasn't been anything worth writing about... Would Benben come if I tried to take it back with me?

choices.text: I think it would rather stay here.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Hey, now you're acting just like Jeht. That thing... Ahem, I mean Benben, can only prove its true worth when it becomes research material for me.

choices.text: Wouldn't you have to change your research topic?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Oh, right! It was the clues on the Stone Slate that led me here. How did I stray so far off my plan?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Benben seems to know this place well, and for some reason, "doors" seem to hold a special place in its heart?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: But if that's true, then which door is its pair?

response.speaker: Benben
response.text: Beep?

choices.text: Benben has three corners, and so do the doors here...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #So Benben's the type that's drawn to something similar to itself, huh? {NICKNAME}, no wonder they say you're an experienced adventurer — you observe everything in such detail.

response.speaker: Benben
response.text: Beep. Bee-eep!

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: *sigh* If only I had a glass of Dandelion Wine right now. Praise be to the oasis!

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: Speaking of "Dandelion," that's also the name of one of our Sumpter Beasts. We named it so because its fur is more fluffy than others, and it sheds so much fur...

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: But I don't think it really likes its name. It shakes fur all over Bonifaz whenever he calls it Dandelion...

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: Could it be that it's just not fond of names from Mondstadt? Would it prefer a name from Sumeru? Something like Tirzad...?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Father seems a little... Maybe he's recalled his past life in the desert. If only he'd tell us some stories of his past at night.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsad
dialogues.text: Every time I stumble upon an oasis, I can't help wondering who put this stretch of water here. It's almost as if they mean to provide a rest stop for adventurers.

dialogues.speaker: Omid
dialogues.text: Where should I open my shop? Port Ormos or Sumeru City?

dialogues.speaker: Omid
dialogues.text: And what should I sell? Wine or coffee?

dialogues.speaker: Omid
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you. Are you leaving? Farewell then, and safe travels! Don't get yourself into a trap or something again!

dialogues.speaker: Mirsad
dialogues.text: Ah, I'm so jealous of you. Unlike us, who can only stand here staring at the sand, you can venture into the depths of the ruins to find out what's hidden in those big guys.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsad
dialogues.text: How I wish I could travel to different places and meet different people, just like you.

dialogues.speaker: Mirsad
dialogues.text: I've always wanted to visit that cathedral in Mondstadt. My boss mentioned it several times, but I never had the chance...
